result.title: CODA: Cohort- and Drift-aware Foundation Model for Multimodal Clinical Reasoning
result.summary: Recent advances in multimodal foundation models have demonstrated strong performance across diverse clinical tasks. However, existing approaches predominantly operate at the individual sample level and fail to model the interplay between population-level cohort patterns and patient-specific variation that underlie real-world clinical reasoning. In practice, clinicians routinely reason through patient cohorts sharing similar demographic, physiological, or pathological characteristics, while accounting for patient-specific deviations from the group prototype. Motivated by this gap, we propose CODA, a cohort- and drift-aware foundation model for multimodal clinical reasoning. CODA explicitly integrates cohort structure into the modeling pipeline through two complementary mechanisms: cohort-aware population stratification and drift-aware individual adaptation. In particular, we leverage reinforcement learning to discover clinically meaningful patient cohorts, and further model each patient's deviation from cohort prototypes as a structured drift signal encoding fine-grained individual heterogeneity. These cohort- and drift-aware representations are incorporated into the foundation model to enable reasoning that is simultaneously informed by population-level patterns and sensitive to individual-level variation. Extensive experiments on real-world electronic health record (EHR) benchmarks demonstrate that CODA achieves consistent effectiveness and strong generalizability across diverse clinical tasks, including closed-QA, open-QA, and report generation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CODA，用强化学习发现具有临床意义的患者队列，并把患者相对队列原型的偏离建模为结构化 drift 信号，将该群体与个体感知表示注入多模态临床基础模型，在 EHR 的 closed-QA、open-QA 与报告生成任务上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 「群体原型 + 个体漂移」的显式结构化表示分解，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态如何同时编码共享结构与个体差异、以及表示几何设计提供可核查线索；但输入为 EHR 而非视觉 token，也无 latent 推理状态生成，迁移性有待人工判断。
